clue.text: Having made a mistake, like fallen gymnast perhaps

blocks.note: first meaning: wrong, mistaken in one's reckoning
second meaning, read literally: a gymnast who has fallen is no longer on the balance beam

explanation.surface: A gymnast slips and tumbles from the apparatus mid-routine, a costly error.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is an idiom for being wrong; read word by word it describes someone who has come off the beam.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone whose reasoning or guess is wide of the truth, like a signal missing its target.

clue.text: Bosses out to dominate one's mind

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or not in the right place, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Managers striving to control their employees' thoughts.
explanation.definitionFit: When a thought fills someone's head continually and will not leave, it preoccupies them entirely.

clue.text: Part of 17 the other way round? That could be a slip

indicators.note: turning the two halves of the referenced name about puts its letters in a new order

blocks.note: the first word of 17 across

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about reversing part of another answer, which might be a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first word as MAN'S FIELD and swap it round to FIELD'S MAN. In cricket, slip is a fielding position beside the wicketkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer stationed at slip is one of the fielding side's players, so a slip is an example of this.

clue.text: Conclusions reached by kings without queens, often

definitions.text: Conclusions reached by kings without queens, often

blocks.clueFragment: Conclusions reached by kings without queens
blocks.note: surface reading: royal decisions made by monarchs who have no consorts
setter's reading: on a chessboard late in a game the queens have usually been swapped off, leaving kings to fight it out

explanation.surface: Unmarried monarchs making decisions without their wives' counsel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conclusions' looks like decisions; it means the final phases of chess games, which typically feature kings with the queens long gone.
explanation.definitionFit: The final stages of chess games, and more generally the closing parts of anything, are conclusions.

clue.text: Gem of Victorian literature

blocks.note: first meaning: a pearly, translucent feldspar stone
second meaning: Wilkie Collins's 1868 detective novel

explanation.surface: A treasured classic from nineteenth-century English writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gem of' reads as praise for a fine book; the gem is a real stone, and a famous Victorian novel shares its name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a milky semi-precious stone, and Wilkie Collins named his early detective story after a stolen diamond so called.

clue.text: Indian drivers whose charges are heavy

definitions.text: Indian drivers whose charges are heavy

blocks.clueFragment: Indian drivers whose charges are heavy
blocks.note: surface reading: taxi drivers in India with steep fares
setter's reading: the charges are the animals in their care, which are elephants and weigh tonnes

explanation.surface: Indian cabbies who overcharge their passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charges' suggests fees; it means the creatures being looked after, and the heaviest beasts driven in India are elephants.
explanation.definitionFit: A mahout is a person who works with, rides and steers an elephant in South and Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Saw German supporting mark

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece that supports another sits beneath it

blocks.note: M is short for mark, the old German currency
Otto is a typical German man's name

explanation.surface: A German man bolstering the value of the Deutschmark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a past tense or a tool; it is the noun meaning a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or proverb, and a maxim adopted as a guiding principle is the same sort of phrase.

clue.text: Shock treatment feared by Damocles?

blocks.note: surface reading: electric shock therapy, or a frightening ordeal
setter's reading: a shock is a mass of hair, and a sword hung over Damocles by a single hair, which he dreaded being severed

explanation.surface: A frightening medical procedure dreaded by a figure from Greek legend.
explanation.walkthrough: Damocles sat beneath a sword suspended by one hair; snipping that hair was the thing to fear. A shock of hair is a thick mop.
explanation.definitionFit: A trim at the barber's is treatment for a thick head of hair, and cutting the hair above Damocles would drop the sword.

clue.text: Objectively, we must have time to find employment

blocks.note: the objective case of we is us
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Speaking frankly, we need time to look for a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objectively' looks like 'impartially'; it is grammar, asking for the object form of the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Employment in the sense of use: the way something is employed or put to work.

clue.text: How, in one case, a dangerous band was spotted

blocks.clueFragment: How, in one case, a dangerous band was spotted
blocks.note: surface reading: police noticing a violent gang during an investigation

blocks.clueFragment: in one case, a dangerous band
blocks.note: setter's reading: in a Sherlock Holmes case, the deadly band turned out to be a swamp adder with markings

explanation.surface: A detective recounts how, during one investigation, a violent gang was noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' seems to mean noticed; it is the definition, meaning marked with spots, and the case is Conan Doyle's story about a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means covered with small marks or flecks, which is what a dotted pattern looks like.

clue.text: Vessel for the fleet

blocks.note: surface reading: a ship belonging to a naval fleet
setter's reading: fleet as an adjective means swift, so this is a craft for those who want speed

explanation.surface: A warship assigned to the navy's fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet' looks like the noun for a group of ships, but here it is the adjective meaning fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A powerboat built for high velocity on water, the kind of craft a swift person would choose.

clue.text: Double portrait

blocks.note: first meaning: an exact likeness of someone, as in 'the spitting ...'
second meaning: a picture or representation of a person

explanation.surface: A painting showing two figures, or a portrait painted twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a person's lookalike and a painted or photographed likeness of them.

clue.text: In South of France, a new home for some Africans

blocks.note: the French word for south, so south as it is said in France
taken as written
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Somewhere in southern France, a group of African migrants finds a new place to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South of France' reads as the Riviera, but the clue wants the French word for south.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudan is an African country, the homeland of the Sudanese people, so it is a home for some of the continent's people.

clue.text: Detect threat to king in random test

blocks.note: to spot something is to notice or detect it
in chess, a king under attack is in check

explanation.surface: A chess player notices an attack on their king during a casual game.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspection made without warning on an item picked at random to see that standards are kept.

clue.text: Short-term gain involving sacrifice - pet goat, possibly?

blocks.clueFragment: Short-term gain involving sacrifice - pet goat, possibly?
blocks.note: surface reading: a quick profit made by giving up a pet goat, perhaps as an offering
setter's reading: a jumbled version of the letters of 'pet goat' spells the thick soup in the biblical phrase, so the whole phrase is literally a muddle of those letters

explanation.surface: Someone trades away the family's pet goat for a quick payout, or offers it up in sacrifice.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis, Esau sold his birthright to Jacob for a bowl of stew; the phrase is the second half of that bargain. 'Mess of' doubles as a signal that the letters of 'pet goat' are jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names something trivial accepted in exchange for a far more valuable thing given up, as Esau did.

clue.text: Lines on which people have descended from pier's edge, perhaps

definitions.text: Lines on which people have descended

indicators.note: perhaps says this is one possible form of the words, so their letters may be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: People climbing down ropes off the end of a seaside jetty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Descended' suggests climbing down; it means being born of ancestors, and the lines are family lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Family trees record lines of ancestry, along which generations have come down from their forebears.

clue.text: Limited cover for a low joint

definitions.text: Limited cover for a low joint

blocks.clueFragment: Limited cover for a low joint
blocks.note: surface reading: poor insurance for a seedy bar or nightclub
setter's reading: the joint lowest on the body is just above the foot, and this garment covers only up to it

explanation.surface: A disreputable bar has only partial insurance.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'low joint' sounds like a seedy dive; it is the bodily joint nearest the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A short sock reaching just to the top of the foot covers that joint and little else.

clue.text: To break strike is very successful achievement

blocks.note: to smash is to break violently
to hit is to strike

explanation.surface: Breaking a workers' strike is presented as a great triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' looks like industrial action; it is the verb meaning to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge popular success, especially a record, show or film, is an achievement that does very well.

clue.text: Author and explorer getting together in novel setting

blocks.note: Katherine Mansfield, the New Zealand short-story writer
Mungo Park, the Scottish explorer of the Niger

explanation.surface: A writer and an adventurer meet up somewhere that might be in a work of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new; it is the noun, a work of fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: This country estate is the house where Jane Austen's 1814 book of the same name takes place.

clue.text: Original clothing supplier

blocks.note: surface reading: an innovative fashion retailer
setter's reading: the first of all, in Eden, where Adam and Eve sewed leaves together to cover themselves

explanation.surface: A creative designer-clothes shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Original' sounds like inventive; it means the very first, and Genesis says Adam and Eve made aprons from the leaves of this plant.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible this plant gave the first humans the leaves for their first garments.

clue.text: Girl upset by insect's feeler

indicators.note: in a down answer, something upset is turned upside down, so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: an ant is an insect
a common girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is distressed by a bug's waving sensor.
explanation.definitionFit: The sensory organ on an insect's head, used for touch and smell, is a feeler.

clue.text: Scientist in the modern style

blocks.note: new means modern
ton is fashionable style, from French

explanation.surface: A researcher working in the latest manner.
explanation.walkthrough: Ton, meaning high fashion, is an old word borrowed from French.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Newton was the English physicist and mathematician who formulated the laws of motion and gravitation.

clue.text: Carrier that enables one to make a clean getaway

definitions.text: Carrier that enables one to make a clean getaway

blocks.clueFragment: Carrier that enables one to make a clean getaway
blocks.note: surface reading: a getaway vehicle that lets a criminal escape without a trace
setter's reading: a pouch holding washing kit lets a traveller go away clean

explanation.surface: A getaway car that lets a robber escape leaving no trace behind.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'clean getaway' is an escape without being caught; here it means going on a trip with soap and flannel to hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterproof toiletry pouch is what a traveller packs for washing, so it lets them stay clean while away.

clue.text: Class instruction

blocks.note: first meaning: a rank or category in biological classification, or a social class
second meaning: a command

explanation.surface: A lesson given in a school class.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a taxonomic rank or grouping and a command given by someone in authority.

clue.text: Heavily hit ring in wrestling tournament

blocks.note: to bash is to hit hard
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A wrestler is pounded in the ring during a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like the wrestling arena; it gives the letter shaped like a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: In Japanese sumo, a basho is one of the official fifteen-day competitions held through the year.

clue.text: A word of comfort in that situation

blocks.note: first meaning: the soothing exclamation often said twice to a crying child
second meaning: at that place or point

explanation.surface: Someone offers a kind word to a person in a difficult position.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means at that place, and the same word is said soothingly, as in consoling someone who is upset.

clue.text: Person sought in game to beat king

blocks.note: to hide someone is to thrash them
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: In a chess match, the player hunting for a way to defeat the opposing monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' as a verb meaning to flog is informal, from tanning someone's hide.
explanation.definitionFit: In hide-and-seek, the players being looked for are those who have concealed themselves.

clue.text: Grim army doctors given a little time extremely far from the front

blocks.note: stern means severe or grim
an MO is a medical officer, so several are MOs
T is the abbreviation for time, a little bit of the word

explanation.surface: Stern-faced military medics are granted a short spell well away from the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Front' suggests a battle line, but here it is the bow of a ship; the answer is a superlative of the back end of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative means nearest the rear of a ship, so it is as far from the bow as possible.

clue.text: Missile soldiers installed in new depot

indicators.note: something new is made fresh, so the word depot is to be rebuilt in another order
things installed in a place are set inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the letters of depot rearranged
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Troops are stationed at a recently built military store.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-propelled underwater weapon fired at ships is a missile.

clue.text: Drop off something in short supply in various quarters

indicators.note: something placed in a group of things sits inside them, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: compass points: south, east and north
a lack is a shortage of something

explanation.surface: Delivering a scarce item to several different neighbourhoods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarters' are the four points of the compass in crosswords, so any of S, E, N and W can be used.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop off means to decline or lessen in pace, which is what slowing or easing up is.
